name: ES Aggressor Granularity Inversion v1
instrument: ES transaction-size signal executed with one MES using recorded MBP-1 quotes
source: Databento GLBX.MDP3 ES trades and MES MBP-1
hypothesis: Aggressor volume loses information about granularity: many small trades and a few large trades can have identical volume. During the pre-close transfer, the side using the larger average aggressive trade reveals greater urgency and impact paid rather than superior information. Price should move against that larger-average-size aggressor side into the close.

signal.buyer_average_size: sum of B trade sizes divided by count of B trade records
signal.seller_average_size: sum of A trade sizes divided by count of A trade records
signal.long_signal: seller average aggressive trade size > buyer average aggressive trade size
signal.short_signal: buyer average aggressive trade size > seller average aggressive trade size
signal.interpretation: fade the side displaying greater average aggressive-order urgency

eligibility.entry_and_exit_quotes: finite, positive, non-crossed recorded MBP-1 bid and ask
eligibility.spread_filter: none; cross the recorded spread regardless of width

execution.entry_time: first MES MBP-1 record at or after 15:30:05 ET
execution.stop: none; one MES and a fixed approximately 29-minute holding period bound exposure
execution.exit_time: first MES MBP-1 record at or after 15:59:45 ET
execution.position_limit: one MES and at most one trade per RTH session

economics.slippage_model: the full recorded MES bid-ask spread is crossed at entry and exit; no additional modeled slippage

lesson: Fading the side with larger average aggressive trade size produced an interesting aggregate result, but essentially all profit came from shorts and 2022. The small 2021 and long-side losses still violate preregistered gates. A short-only or side-conditioned granularity engine is prohibited.
holdout_policy: 2024-2025 was not evaluated because the unchanged rule failed its development gates.
prohibited_posthoc_changes: following rather than fading the larger-average-size side
using medians, maxima, percentiles, or trade-size thresholds
combining average size with net flow, price direction, or trade-count direction
changing the trade or quote windows
weekday, volatility, volume, or regime filters
